picks.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non-Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes.

sections.objective: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study.
sections.methods: In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate.
sections.results: A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported.
sections.conclusion: Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. (Funded by Dexcom; CONNECT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06601166.).

picks.title: Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury.

sections.objective: The preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90.
sections.results: The trial was stopped early after sequential interim analyses showed a sustained signal of higher mortality with intermittent hemodialysis than with continuous renal-replacement therapy. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively. Kaplan-Meier mortality estimates at day 90 were 63.3% and 53.6% (hazard ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.63). The most common complication potentially related to acute kidney injury or renal-replacement therapy was hypotension, which occurred in 179 patients (68.8%) in the intermittent group and in 183 patients (66.5%) in the continuous group.
sections.conclusion: Among critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy, intermittent hemodialysis as the initial treatment approach was not shown to be noninferior to continuous renal-replacement therapy with respect to major adverse kidney events by day 90 and was associated with higher mortality. (Funded by the French Ministry of Health; ICRAKI ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06032884.).

picks.title: Nearly half of reef-building corals face elevated relative risk of extinction.
picks.abstract: Coral reefs are diverse marine ecosystems that provide ecological functions and economic and social benefits across over 100 tropical countries. Warming driven by climate change is a primary threat to coral reefs and is increasing the frequency of global coral bleaching events. Here we reassessed the IUCN Red List status of 892 reef-building coral species, first assessed in 2008 1. Because species-level population trends are unavailable for most reef-building corals, population reductions were inferred using proxies based on global coral cover trends and projected annual severe bleaching under SSP2-4.5, both over three decades, adjusted using trait-based estimates of species vulnerability. Of the 774 species with sufficient data to be assessed, 340 (44%) were classified as threatened under IUCN Red List criteria. Thirty-three species were assessed as Critically Endangered, 251 as Endangered, and 56 as Vulnerable, most due to risk of population reduction associated with projected thermal stress. These findings predate the three hottest years on record and the fourth global coral bleaching event (2023-2025), and the first exceedance for an annual mean of the 1.5oC global warming threshold. The findings reinforce the importance of limiting further warming to maintain coral biodiversity and reef ecosystem function. The Red List assesses the relative extinction risk of species, whereby species are placed in categories of increasing risk by comparing their population size, decline and geographic range against standardised thresholds. The Red List does not predict whether or when a species may go extinct. As the ranges of coral species remain under-surveyed, future assessments would be strengthened by species-level population data and thermal-stress and recovery metrics that better capture range-representative dynamics.

picks.title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3.
picks.abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. Here, we describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which employs free atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active site architecture incorporating a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases we obtain active catalysts in zero shot 96 construct design campaigns.

picks.title: Evaluation of the accuracy, completeness, and compliance of current summary reporting of adverse events to the Food and Drug Administration using the manufacturer and user facility device experience (MAUDE) database: cross sectional study.

sections.objective: To evaluate the accuracy and completeness of adverse event summary reports for medical devices and compliance of the reports with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) requirements.
sections.methods: Cross sectional study. All adverse event summary reports filed in MAUDE from July 2019 to June 2025.
sections.results: 6308 summary reports were submitted to MAUDE containing 159 503 adverse events. Use of summary reports increased from 808 to 1757 between 2020 and 2024, a factor of 1.21 per year (P<0.001). Most (91%) adverse events in summary reports were for class 3 high risk devices. Summary reports lacked descriptions of potential device related problems: 57% of reports denoted an "adverse event without identified device or use problem" and 38% of reports selected "insufficient information" in the device problem code data field. Manufacturers incorrectly checked "N" (no) in the summary report (Y/N, reporting yes/no) field for 694 summary reports (11%) and erroneously listed "n=1" under the number of events field for 423 summary reports (7%), causing an undercount of 11 902 adverse events. The majority (55%) of summary reports failed to comply with the FDA reporting deadline of 30 days after the manufacturer became aware of the adverse event.
sections.conclusion: Adverse event summary reports in MAUDE are frequently incomplete, inaccurate, and delayed. Improvements are needed to ensure timely identification of device safety signals and uphold FDA transparency standards.
sections.other: The FDA manufacturer and user facility device experience (MAUDE) database. Identification of device problem codes, appropriate identification as summary reports in the submission form, concordance between the number of events data field and the report narrative, and compliance with FDA reporting deadlines.

picks.title: Structural variant detection across sequencing technologies.
picks.abstract: Structural variants (SVs) are a major source of genomic diversity, yet their discovery remains challenging due to repetitive genomic contexts, alignment ambiguity and the trade-off between sequencing cost and read length. Here we introduce HitSV, which implements repetitiveness- and signature-density-aware breakpoint recognition coupled with precise haplotype-resolved local assembly, thereby enabling base-resolution SV reconstruction and genotyping in various sequencing technologies. On the HG002 benchmark, HitSV achieved 15-72% (long read), 10-36% (short read) and 12% (hybrid sequencing), respectively, higher genotype F1 scores than state-of-the-art SV callers. Applied to the 1KGP phase 4 cohort, HitSV expanded the SV callset by 31.5%, substantially reshaping allele-frequency landscapes. In a large Chinese long-read cohort, HitSV uncovered tandem-repeat-mobile-element composite arrays as a prevalent, multi-allelic class of complex SVs, highlighting composite repeat architectures as an important and previously underrecognized contributor to human structural variation.

picks.title: 8 weeks versus 12 weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir for treatment-naive, non-cirrhotic, chronic hepatitis C (RESOLVE): a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial in India.

sections.objective: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection without cirrhosis can be treated with 12 weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir combination therapy. We aimed to assess whether a shorter 8-week treatment regimen of this combination was non-inferior to the standard 12-week regimen in successfully clearing HCV infection in HCV-infected patients without evidence of cirrhosis.
sections.methods: RESOLVE was a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial, conducted in five publicly funded hospitals in India. We randomly assigned (1:1) treatment-naive adults (aged ≥18 years) with non-cirrhotic HCV mono-infection to receive sofosbuvir 400 mg and velpatasvir 100 mg (orally, daily) for either 8 weeks or 12 weeks. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants with sustained virological response-ie, absence of quantifiable HCV RNA at 12 weeks after treatment completion (SVR12), with 95% assumed proportion with 12-week treatment, 5% non-inferiority margin, 2·5% one-sided alpha error, and 90% study power in the per-protocol population. The trial was registered with the Clinical Trial Registry of India, CTRI/2022/03/041368, and is complete.
sections.results: Between May 15, 2022, and Sept 10, 2024, we screened 1620 participants, of whom 880 (54·3%) were enrolled in the study and randomly assigned to the 12-week (n=437 [50%]) or 8-week (n=443 [50%]) groups. 455 (52%) participants were women, 425 (48%) were men, and the median age was 35 years (IQR 28 to 47). 816 (93%) participants completed the intended 12-week (401 [92%] of 437) or 8-week (415 [94%] of 443) treatment and SVR12 testing. On per-protocol analysis, the proportion reaching SVR12 with 8-week treatment (410/415; 98·8% [95% CI 97·2 to 99·6]) was non-inferior to 12-week treatment (397/401; 99·0% [97·5 to 99·7]), with a risk difference of 0·2% (-1·5 to 1·9). Further, on intention-to-treat analysis, the proportion of participants reaching SVR12 with 8-week treatment (414/443; 93·5% [90·9 to 95·5]) was non-inferior to 12-week treatment (401/437; 91·8% [88·8 to 94·2]) with a risk difference of -1·7% (-5·2 to 1·9). No participant had any drug-related serious adverse event or drug discontinuation due to an adverse event.
sections.conclusion: An 8-week regimen of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir was similar in efficacy to the standard 12-week treatment in individuals with chronic HCV infection without cirrhosis. This finding supports shortening the duration of treatment in such patients.

picks.title: A phenome-wide structural variant map from 467,152 UK Biobank genomes.
picks.abstract: Structural variants (SVs) are large (>50 base pairs) genomic rearrangements that can significantly influence human phenotypes, yet their contribution to health and disease remains undercharacterized. We conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) of 1.6 million SVs identified in whole-genome sequencing data from 467,152 UK Biobank participants, across 13,322 binary, 2,018 quantitative, and 2,923 plasma protein traits. Of these, 82.25% of SVs were outside the detectable range of prior copy-number variant studies. Protein quantitative trait loci analysis linked 3,467 SVs to 1,690 proteins, with effects dependent on SV type and location. In SV-PheWAS, we detected 28,184 associations with human health outcomes. Notably, we uncovered rare SVs with strong phenotypic effects. Furthermore, we show that at known genome-wide association study loci, 32.21% of associated SVs overlapped functional genomic regions. This study underscores the underestimated role of SVs in human genetics and their potential to advance understanding of human biology and drug discovery.

items.title: Prognostic Value of Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve From a Large Nationwide Cohort.

sections.objective: The diagnostic value of coronary computed tomography angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR-CT) in stable coronary artery disease is well established. The prognostic value of predicting future cardiovascular events is less clear, as studies are limited by small populations, variable measurement points, composite outcomes, and short follow-up. A nationwide cohort of coronary computed tomography angiography with 3-year follow-up was used to examine the association between FFR-CT measurements and future cardiovascular events.
sections.methods: Patients receiving coronary computed tomography angiography and clinically indicated FFR-CT analysis (HeartFlow) for stable coronary artery disease between 2017 and 2020 at 27 sites across England were included. Lowest per-patient stenosis-specific and distal vessel FFR-CT measurements were related to individual outcomes of myocardial infarction (MI), cardiovascular mortality, all-cause mortality, and revascularization. FFR-CT measurements were divided into subgroups to investigate for a gradient of risk: normal FFR-CT (>0.8), borderline (0.71-0.8), reduced (0.51-0.7), and severely reduced (≤0.5).
sections.results: In total, 7836 patients aged 63 (56.0-71.0), 37.4% women, underwent FFR-CT analysis. Stenosis-specific FFR-CT was associated with future MI (hazard ratio [HR], 2.08-5.73; P<0.001), cardiovascular death (HR, 1.51-3.40; P<0.001), all-cause death (HR, 1.01-1.58; P=0.01), and revascularization (HR, 4.79-24.48; P<0.001), with lower FFR-CT values associated with incrementally greater risk. After adjusting for cardiovascular risk factors and coronary stenosis severity (Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System), stenosis-specific FFR-CT≤0.7 was associated with MI (adjusted HR, 2.94-3.39; P<0.001), ≤0.5 with cardiovascular death (adjusted HR, 2.92; P=0.02), all-cause death (adjusted HR, 1.49; P=0.045), and ≤0.8 with revascularization (adjusted HR, 3.02-9.42; P<0.001). The addition of FFR-CT improved discrimination for MI or cardiovascular death compared with a risk factor and stenosis severity model (C index, 0.783; ∆C index, 0.012; P<0.001). An FFR-CT value of 0.67 defined the optimal cutoff for risk of future cardiovascular events. Distal-vessel FFR-CT was associated with outcomes similar to stenosis-specific FFR-CT. Stenosis-specific and distal-vessel FFR-CT discordance was common (36.4%), but when stenosis-specific FFR-CT was normal, event rates were low (1.5% at 3 years for MI or cardiovascular death).
sections.conclusion: FFR-CT is associated with the individual outcomes of MI, cardiovascular death, and all-cause death independent of risk factors and stenosis severity, with lower FFR-CT values associated with worse outcomes. Reduced and severely reduced FFR-CT have the strongest association with future cardiovascular events, with a value of 0.67 defining the optimal risk threshold.

items.title: Women's Kidney Health in Focus: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
items.abstract: Chronic kidney disease is a global epidemic affecting ≈10% of adults worldwide. Women have a higher prevalence of chronic kidney disease than men yet are less likely to progress to kidney failure, to initiate dialysis, or to receive a kidney transplantation, underscoring the influence of biological sex on chronic kidney disease development, progression, treatment response, and outcomes. Women may also respond differently from men to pharmacological therapies, but they remain underrepresented in clinical trials, limiting the evidence base for sex-specific kidney care. Preclinical evidence implicates a role for estrogen receptor signaling in renal physiology and pathophysiology. Women with chronic kidney disease are at increased risk for adverse pregnancy outcomes and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and pregnancy complications can also increase future chronic kidney disease risk. Menopause and aging accelerate chronic kidney disease progression in women as a result of declining estradiol and shifts in kidney estrogen receptor profiles. Endocrine and metabolic disorders such as polycystic ovary syndrome increase susceptibility to chronic kidney disease. Family planning, prepregnancy counseling, and antenatal care are essential to support reproductive health in women with chronic kidney disease. Because chronic kidney disease and cardiovascular disease are tightly intertwined, chronic kidney disease is also a leading contributor to cardiovascular mortality in women. Advancing precision kidney medicine for women requires equitable access to kidney care, embedding assessment of reproductive health in chronic care, trial design with adequate power that includes both women and men, and mechanistic studies linking reproductive health to long-term cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease development and progression.

items.title: State of Cardiovascular Disease and Stroke in Hispanic/Latino Adults in the United States: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease became the leading cause of death among Hispanic individuals in the United States in 2022. Hispanic adults experience a disproportionate burden of cardiometabolic risk factors, including obesity, diabetes, and dyslipidemia. Hispanic populations are highly heterogeneous, with substantial variations in genetic ancestry and sociocultural influences that shape cardiovascular disease risk and outcomes. The "Hispanic paradox," describing lower cardiovascular disease mortality despite higher risk factor burden, is increasingly recognized as an oversimplification that does not apply uniformly across Hispanic heritage groups, sexes, or disease types. Disaggregated data reveal substantial differences in risk profiles and disease burden among Hispanic heritage groups, emphasizing the limitations of treating this population as a monolithic unit. Recent evidence demonstrates widening disparities in hypertension control, obesity, diabetes, and metabolic diseases among Hispanic populations, threatening this prior mortality advantage. Advancing cardiovascular and equitable health will require developing a deeper understanding of the unique drivers of cardiovascular disease within diverse Hispanic communities, addressing barriers such as language and insurance access, and implementing culturally tailored interventions and policies. This scientific statement summarizes current cardiovascular disease epidemiology in Hispanic populations, emphasizing heritage group variation and social and structural determinants of health, and presents strategies to improve prevention and healthcare delivery. Key priorities for advancing cardiovascular health in Hispanic adults include expanding disaggregated data collection, increasing representation in research, and ensuring equitable implementation of precision medicine approaches, including genomics, multi-omics, and artificial intelligence, while addressing environmental exposures, psychosocial stressors, and policy-related drivers of risk in order to achieve the American Heart Association's 2028 Impact Goals to advancing health and hope for everyone, everywhere.

items.title: An Updated Evidence Assessment of the Genetic Causes of Dilated Cardiomyopathy.

sections.objective: Evidence of the diverse genetic architecture of dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) continues to emerge and requires reassessment of the clinical relevance of implicated disease genes. Building on the 2019-2020 Clinical Genome Resource evaluation, the DCM gene curation expert panel reconvened in 2024-2025 to conduct a reassessment of genes in DCM.
sections.methods: The Clinical Genome Resource semiquantitative clinical validity classification framework was applied with specifications to DCM to classify genes into categories on the basis of strength of published evidence for a DCM phenotype. Previously curated genes were reassessed, and newly reported gene-disease-mode of inheritance (MOI) relationships, termed "curations," were evaluated.
sections.results: Sixty-eight genes were evaluated, inclusive of 72 unique gene-disease-MOI relationships across 51 previously evaluated and 17 newly assessed genes. Thirty-five curations were classified as high evidence (16 Definitive, 10 Strong, 9 Moderate), increasing by 16 from the prior assessment. Nine newly assessed genes were classified as high evidence: BAG5, FLII, LMOD2, MYLK3, MYZAP, NRAP, PPA2, PPP1R13L, and RPL3L. Twelve genes (11 newly appraised) were rated as high evidence with an autosomal recessive (AR) MOI. Five reevaluated genes from 2019-2020 had clinically significant changes in classification. Except for JPH2, for which curation was modified to separate autosomal dominant and AR MOI curations, clinically significant changes involved upgrades from low- to high-evidence categories (PLEKHM2, PRDM16, TBX20, TNNI3K), demonstrating the robustness of the Clinical Genome Resource gene curation process over time. An additional 29 gene-disease-MOI curations were classified as Limited, including 6 newly evaluated genes and 1 new MOI for a previously evaluated gene, MYBPC3-AR; 4 were classified as No Known Disease Relationship, and remained Disputed. Four previously evaluated genes were curated for both AD and AR MOIs: JPH2 (AD-Strong, AR-Limited), LDB3 (AD-Limited, AR-Strong), MYBPC3 (AD-Limited, AR-Limited), and TNNI3 (AD- and AR- Strong).
sections.conclusion: With substantial new evidence, the genetic architecture of DCM has rapidly expanded. This updated assessment of genes reported in DCM yielded 35 high-evidence curations, an increase from 19 only 5 years ago. The results of this evidence-based evaluation process inform clinical interpretation of genetic information in the care of DCM patients and families.

items.title: HNRNPK Lactylation Amplifies Inflammation and Exacerbates Myocardial Ischemia/Reperfusion Injury by Regulating Jag2 Splicing.

sections.objective: Myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury triggers profound metabolic reprogramming and lactate accumulation. However, how this metabolic stress regulates inflammatory gene expression remains poorly understood. We hypothesized that lactylation, a lactate-derived posttranslational modification, links metabolic stress to aberrant RNA splicing and cardiac inflammation through the RNA-binding protein HNRNPK (heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein K).
sections.methods: We analyzed atrial tissues from patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass and murine ischemia/reperfusion hearts to assess lactylation dynamics. Lactylation-specific proteomics, RNA sequencing, and crosslinking and immunoprecipitation followed by quantitative polymerase chain reaction were used to identify HNRNPK targets. Mechanisms were defined using site-directed mutagenesis (HNRNPK-K405R), isoform-specific overexpression, and a therapeutic splice-switching antisense oligonucleotide in mice and cardiomyocytes.
sections.results: Reperfusion significantly increased global protein lactylation in human and murine myocardium. Proteomics identified HNRNPK as a key target, specifically lactylated at lysine 405 (K405la). Ischemia-induced K405la promoted HNRNPK binding to Jag2 pre-mRNA, suppressing exon 10 skipping and shifting splicing from the Jag2 (Jagged2) short (Jag2-S) to the long (Jag2-L) isoform. Jag2-L, but not Jag2-S, exhibited high affinity for Notch1, hyperactivating Notch-NF-κB (nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells) signaling and exacerbating inflammation and infarct size. Mice expressing a lactylation-deficient variant (HNRNPK-K405R) were protected from ischemia/reperfusion injury. Treatment with a specific antisense oligonucleotide (Jag2-i9) that blocks the HNRNPK-Jag2 interaction prevented Jag2-L production and attenuated cardiac dysfunction.
sections.conclusion: HNRNPK lactylation acts as a metabolic sensor coupling lactate accumulation to pathogenic Jag2 splicing. Targeting this metabolic-splicing axis offers a precise therapeutic strategy to limit inflammation and preserve cardiac function in ischemic heart disease.

items.title: Effect of Aficamten on Cardiac Structure and Function in Patients With Symptomatic Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.

sections.objective: Aficamten significantly improved both functional capacity and patient-reported health status in patients with symptomatic nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled ACACIA-HCM trial (Assessment Comparing Aficamten to Placebo on Cardiac Endpoints in Adults with Non-Obstructive HCM; NCT06081894). Serial echocardiographic examinations may provide insights into the mechanisms underlying the therapeutic effect of aficamten in this prespecified exploratory analysis.
sections.methods: Symptomatic patients with nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy were randomized 1:1 to receive aficamten (range, 5-20 mg, titration based on left ventricular [LV] ejection fraction) or placebo for up to 72 weeks (end of treatment). The effect of aficamten on echocardiographic measures at 36 weeks (time of primary end point) and end of treatment was assessed with linear regression models adjusted for baseline values, intracavity obstruction, and baseline atrial fibrillation.
sections.results: Among 517 participants (mean±SD: age, 55±16 years; 54% female, 75% White, 13% Asian), mean baseline LV ejection fraction was 68±4% with abnormal measures of diastolic function. Compared with placebo, aficamten decreased LV ejection fraction (-4.6% [-5.5, -3.6]; P<0.001) at 36 weeks and increased LV volumes. Aficamten improved measures of diastolic function, including lateral e' and septal e' velocities, at 36 weeks (0.9 cm/s [0.6, 1.2] and 0.7 cm/s [0.4, 0.9], respectively; P<0.001 for both) and at end of treatment (0.9 cm/s [0.5, 1.2] and 0.9 cm/s [0.6, 1.1], respectively; P<0.001 for both) and septal E/e' by end of treatment (-1.4 [-2.1, -0.6]; P<0.001, respectively). Peak tricuspid regurgitation velocity improved at 36 weeks (-10.4 cm/s [-19.9, -1.0]; P=0.030) with a sustained effect through end of treatment. Left atrial volume index did not significantly improve at 36 weeks (-1.3 [95% CI, -2.6, 0.04]; P=0.06) but showed a trend towards improvement with longer treatment exposure (-1.7 [-3.2, -0.3]; P=0.022). Aficamten demonstrated incremental improvements in measures of LV structure and function compared to placebo as doses were increased, with improvement in diastolic indices evident by week 2 of titration.
sections.conclusion: In patients with nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, aficamten improved echocardiographic measures of diastolic function. These findings suggest that the benefits of aficamten extend beyond the effects of LV outflow tract gradient reduction observed in prior studies.

items.title: Collapse and Thrombosis of an Iliac Branch Endovascular Device Following Blunt Force Trauma.
items.abstract: Iliac branch endovascular device thrombosis following blunt force trauma has rarely been reported. We describe an 81-year-old man who developed proximal aortobiiliac endograft collapse with subsequent thrombosis after blunt force trauma occurring two months following endovascular aneurysm repair. The patient delayed vascular follow-up for one year and later presented at routine surveillance with progressive bilateral hip and buttock claudication. Despite chronic therapeutic anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation, the patient developed progressive thrombosis with ischemic symptoms. The case highlights a rare mechanical cause of post-EVAR aortoiliac thrombosis and demonstrates the importance of early vascular imaging and consultation following traumatic injury in post-EVAR patients.

items.title: Volumetric Analysis versus Diameter Measurement for Early Detection of Post-EVAR Sac Progression.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo compare diameter- and volume-based surveillance after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and determine whether volumetric sac assessment identifies postoperative remodeling not captured by conventional maximum diameter measurement.MethodsThis retrospective single-center study included 383 patients who underwent elective EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm between January 2016 and April 2024. All patients had preoperative and postoperative computed tomography angiography and at least 1 year of follow-up. Maximum sac diameter, total aneurysm sac volume, thrombus volume, thrombus density, neck morphology, and other anatomical variables were assessed using standardized morphometric and three-dimensional morphovolumetric measurements. Sac dynamics were classified by diameter criteria (≥5 mm decrease, stable, or ≥5 mm increase) and volumetric criteria (>10% decrease, stable, or >10% increase).ResultsEndoleaks occurred in 26.1% of patients (n = 100), and secondary interventions were required in 14.1% (n = 54), with a mean time to reintervention of 21.7 ± 10 months. At final follow-up, 74.7% demonstrated sac diameter reduction, 18.5% were stable, and 6.8% had enlargement, whereas volumetric analysis showed shrinkage in 81.7%, stability in 6.0%, and enlargement in 12.3%. At 1, 6, and 12 months, cohort mean diameter changed by -0.6%, -3.1%, and -6.5% from baseline, respectively, while cohort mean volume changed by -0.5%, -5.7%, and -12.5%. Among diameter-stable sacs, 32.4% enlarged volumetrically and 38.0% regressed volumetrically. In enlarging sacs, a 10% volume increase corresponded to an approximately 4 mm diameter increase (R2 = 0.72; P < 0.001); this 4 mm value was a regression estimate, not the diameter threshold used for sac classification. Preoperative morphometric and morphovolumetric variables were associated with endoleak and secondary intervention in exploratory analyses.ConclusionVolumetric sac analysis identified additional postoperative remodeling beyond maximum diameter measurement, particularly in apparently stable sacs. A practical surveillance strategy combining rapid diameter-based screening with selective volumetric analysis in stable, borderline, or clinically suspicious cases may improve recognition of adverse sac behavior without requiring routine volumetry in every follow-up study.

items.title: The conserved NUS-1/DHDDS-1 complex links N-glycosylation to lipid and lysosomal homeostasis in C. elegans.
items.abstract: N-glycosylation is essential for proteome integrity, yet the systemic roles of the cis-prenyltransferase (cis-PT) complex remain poorly defined. Using Caenorhabditis elegans, we demonstrate that this complex is a dual regulator of global lipid and lysosomal homeostasis. Mechanistically, NUS-1 physically associates with the core oligosaccharyltransferase (OST) complex to coordinate N-glycan transfer. Loss of NUS-1/DHDDS-1 triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress, lysosomal collapse, and systemic lipopenia. This lipid defect arises from impaired N-glycosylation of the SREBP cleavage-activating protein (SCAP). cis-PT deficiency causes unglycosylated SCAP to undergo massive degradation and absolute physical entrapment within the ER, preventing SREBP nuclear translocation and downstream lipid synthesis. Furthermore, pathogenic mutations cause dysfunction through distinct molecular mechanisms: pocket integrity disruption or catalytic impairment. These findings uncover an essential crosstalk between protein glycosylation and global lipid metabolism, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding the systemic pathophysiology of congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG).

items.title: Predictors of Surveillance Imaging Non-compliance Among Patients with TEVAR for Blunt Thoracic Aortic Injury.
items.abstract: ObjectivesBlunt Thoracic Aortic Injury (BTAI) is the second leading cause of death for patients with blunt trauma. Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) has become the standard of care for high-grade BTAI, reducing morbidity and mortality while requiring long-term surveillance imaging to ensure graft integrity and prevent future complications. However, adherence to this protocol is poor. Previous studies evaluating the factors associated with post-operative imaging non-compliance have yielded conflicting results. This study aimed to evaluate predictors of post-TEVAR non-compliance inpatients presenting with BTAI.MethodsA retrospective study on 23 patients was conducted using a single institution Aortic Center Database (2015-2025). Inclusion criteria included patients who were age >18 years and underwent TEVAR for BTAI. Demographic, comorbidity, hospital course, and follow-up data were collected. The Distressed Communities Index (DCI) score was derived from patient's home address ZIP code. Time-to-event analysis defined loss to follow up (LTFU) for vascular imaging as the failure event. Patients were censored at death or if compliant through 1 year following the index TEVAR. Statistical analysis included chi-square, t-tests, and Kaplan-Meier survival.ResultsBased on this single-center review on TEVAR follow-up for BTAI, sex, race, and hospital length of stay did not impact compliance. Medical comorbidities were also non-significant. Patients who presented with a lower injury severity score (P = 0.02) and lived more than 20 miles from their follow-up appointment (P = 0.02) were more likely to be LTFU. While the type of facility was not impactful, all patients who were discharged to a non-home location were LTFU. Interestingly, DCI and insurance status had no impact on follow-up non-compliance.ConclusionsThis study supports the development of targeted, patient-centered surveillance strategies, especially amongst rural populations and those discharged to a non-home location. To fully understand this complex problem, further investigation using a larger database may be indicated.

items.title: Outcomes After Major Amputation in Octogenarians.
items.abstract: BackgroundMajor lower extremity amputations, defined as above-ankle amputations, are morbid and significantly life-changing. Older patients may be more susceptible to poor outcomes. Our goal was to assess the short- and long-term outcomes of major amputations in octogenarians.MethodsA retrospective single-center chart review was performed on all octogenarian patients who underwent a major amputation at a safety-net hospital between 2014-2023. Demographics, operative characteristics, postoperative outcomes, and 30-day and 1-year outcomes were collected and analyzed. Multivariable binary logistic regression evaluated factors associated with 1-year mortality. Fisher's exact test evaluated univariate categorical comparisons because of small cell frequencies.Results56 octogenarian patients underwent a major amputation: 96.4% underwent an amputation for chronic limb-threatening ischemia while 3.6% of patients had acute limb ischemia. Above-knee and below-knee amputations accounted for 73.2 and 26.8% of procedures, respectively; 10.6% were guillotine amputations. Intensive care unit (ICU) admission was required in 26.3% of cases, and total mean hospital length of stay (LOS) was 13.7 days. Postoperatively, 55.4% were discharged to a skilled nursing facility, 17.9% patients to an acute rehab facility, and 12.5% to home with assistance. Thirty-day emergency department use rate was 14.3%, and hospital readmission rate was 12.5%. Most patients (83.9%) were non-ambulatory at 1-year. In-hospital mortality was 8.9%, 30-day mortality was 14.3%, and 1-year mortality was 35.7%. Univariate analyses demonstrated no statistically significant differences among evaluated variables. Multivariable analysis of 1-year mortality was also not statistically significant.ConclusionMajor amputations in octogenarians are highly morbid with high ICU utilization and prolonged LOS with frequent discharge to acute care facilities. About one-third of patients are not alive at 1-year. These findings suggest the need to identify opportunities for improvement in this high-risk patient population undergoing amputations, such as early revascularization, aggressive rehabilitation in concert with geriatrician collaboration, medical optimization, and improved goals-of-care discussions.

items.title: Snare Assisted Guiding Catheter Stabilization for Left Internal Carotid Artery Access via Right Distal Radial Approach.
items.abstract: Transradial approach (TRA) is increasingly adopted in neurointervention. However, distal system advancement to the left internal carotid artery (ICA) via a right radial approach can be technically challenging, particularly when a small-caliber system is required. We report a case in which a stable guiding system was established via a right distal radial approach by capturing the guiding catheter with a snare and applying traction. Despite marked ICA tortuosity, distal advancement of the distal access catheter and system push during flow diverter deployment were successfully achieved. This single-case technical experience suggests that snare-assisted guiding catheter stabilization may represent one technical option for addressing support limitations in challenging TRA procedures.

items.title: 8 weeks versus 12 weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir for treatment-naive, non-cirrhotic, chronic hepatitis C (RESOLVE): a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial in India.

sections.objective: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection without cirrhosis can be treated with 12 weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir combination therapy. We aimed to assess whether a shorter 8-week treatment regimen of this combination was non-inferior to the standard 12-week regimen in successfully clearing HCV infection in HCV-infected patients without evidence of cirrhosis.
sections.methods: RESOLVE was a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial, conducted in five publicly funded hospitals in India. We randomly assigned (1:1) treatment-naive adults (aged ≥18 years) with non-cirrhotic HCV mono-infection to receive sofosbuvir 400 mg and velpatasvir 100 mg (orally, daily) for either 8 weeks or 12 weeks. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants with sustained virological response-ie, absence of quantifiable HCV RNA at 12 weeks after treatment completion (SVR12), with 95% assumed proportion with 12-week treatment, 5% non-inferiority margin, 2·5% one-sided alpha error, and 90% study power in the per-protocol population. The trial was registered with the Clinical Trial Registry of India, CTRI/2022/03/041368, and is complete.
sections.results: Between May 15, 2022, and Sept 10, 2024, we screened 1620 participants, of whom 880 (54·3%) were enrolled in the study and randomly assigned to the 12-week (n=437 [50%]) or 8-week (n=443 [50%]) groups. 455 (52%) participants were women, 425 (48%) were men, and the median age was 35 years (IQR 28 to 47). 816 (93%) participants completed the intended 12-week (401 [92%] of 437) or 8-week (415 [94%] of 443) treatment and SVR12 testing. On per-protocol analysis, the proportion reaching SVR12 with 8-week treatment (410/415; 98·8% [95% CI 97·2 to 99·6]) was non-inferior to 12-week treatment (397/401; 99·0% [97·5 to 99·7]), with a risk difference of 0·2% (-1·5 to 1·9). Further, on intention-to-treat analysis, the proportion of participants reaching SVR12 with 8-week treatment (414/443; 93·5% [90·9 to 95·5]) was non-inferior to 12-week treatment (401/437; 91·8% [88·8 to 94·2]) with a risk difference of -1·7% (-5·2 to 1·9). No participant had any drug-related serious adverse event or drug discontinuation due to an adverse event.
sections.conclusion: An 8-week regimen of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir was similar in efficacy to the standard 12-week treatment in individuals with chronic HCV infection without cirrhosis. This finding supports shortening the duration of treatment in such patients.

items.title: Cardiovascular safety of orforglipron versus insulin glargine in adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4): a phase 3, event-driven, randomised, open-label, non-inferiority, active comparator trial.

sections.objective: Orforglipron is an oral, non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist. While some peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists have established cardiovascular benefit, the cardiovascular safety of non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists has not been studied. This study aimed to compare the effect of orforglipron with insulin glargine on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in individuals with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight who are at increased risk for cardiovascular events.
sections.methods: This event-driven, phase 3, multicentre, randomised, open-label, active comparator, parallel-group study was conducted in 317 sites across 16 countries and territories. Adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk with glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) concentrations between 7·0% and 10·5% (53-91 mmol/mol) and a BMI of 25 kg/m2 or more, treated with up to three glucose-lowering medications (metformin, a sulfonylurea, and/or an SGLT2 inhibitor), were randomly assigned (1:1) to oral orforglipron maximum tolerated dose (up to 36 mg capsule [equivalent to 17·2 mg tablet]) or injectable titrated insulin glargine, each administered once daily. All participants had established cardiovascular or chronic kidney disease. The primary outcome was time to occurrence of four-component major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-4), including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for unstable angina. Non-inferiority of orforglipron to insulin glargine was declared if the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI for the hazard ratio (HR; orforglipron vs insulin glargine) was less than 1·8. The primary endpoint and other safety endpoints were assessed in all participants who took at least one dose of assigned treatment using all datapoints from baseline until withdrawal or study completion, regardless of treatment adherence. This trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05803421) and is completed.
sections.results: Between May 1, 2023, and Sept 5, 2024, 2749 participants were randomly assigned (1371 to orforglipron and 1378 to insulin glargine). 1032 (38%) participants were female and 1717 (62·5%) male. 2362 (85·9%) participants had established cardiovascular disease and 1033 (37·6%) had chronic kidney disease. Mean baseline age, HbA1c, and BMI were 63·1 years (SD 9·9), 8·2% (1·0), and 33 kg/m2 (6·2), respectively. Over a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome occurred in 57 (4·2%) of 1358 orforglipron participants and 67 (5·0%) of 1343 insulin glargine participants, showing non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4 (HR 0·84; 95% CI 0·59-1·20; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Gastrointestinal adverse events were reported in 851 (62·1%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 193 (14·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants; clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia (glucose <3 mmol/L [54 mg/dL]) occurred in 93 (6·8%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 260 (19·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants. 62 deaths were reported during the study: 19 (1·4%) of 1371 participants receiving orforglipron and 43 (3·2%) of 1355 participants receiving insulin glargine; all deaths except one (in the insulin glargine group) were deemed unrelated to treatment.
sections.conclusion: In people with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk, the cardiovascular safety of orforglipron was confirmed by demonstrating non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent adverse event and most common reason for orforglipron treatment discontinuation with orforglipron, while clinically significant hypoglycaemia occurred less frequently with orforglipron than with insulin glargine. These findings support orforglipron as a potential once-daily, oral treatment option with established cardiovascular safety in people with type 2 diabetes and increased cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of garetosmab, an activin A-blocking antibody, in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (OPTIMA): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is an ultrarare genetic disorder resulting in progressive heterotopic ossification of ligaments, tendons, and muscles, leading to disability and early mortality. FOP is caused by heterozygous gain-of-function mutations in the activin receptor type 1A, allowing this receptor to be aberrantly activated by activin A (ActA), which normally inhibits this receptor, thus driving heterotopic bone formation. In preclinical models and an earlier phase 2 trial (LUMINA-1) in FOP, an antibody blocking ActA (garetosmab) prevented heterotopic ossification. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of garetosmab in adults living with FOP.
sections.methods: OPTIMA is a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial conducted at 18 study sites across 16 countries and regions. Participants aged 18 years or older with FOP were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to monthly intravenous placebo, garetosmab 3 mg/kg, or garetosmab 10 mg/kg. Randomisation was stratified by baseline Cumulative Analogue Joint Involvement Scale score and previous participation in the LUMINA-1 study. The primary efficacy and safety endpoints were total number of new heterotopic bone lesions at week 56 and treatment-emergent adverse events of special interest (AESIs) through week 56, analysed in all randomised participants who received at least one dose of the study drug. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05394116); the trial is active (completed primary endpoint) but not recruiting participants.
sections.results: Between Nov 21, 2022, and July 4, 2024, 63 participants were enrolled and randomly assigned (placebo, n=21; garetosmab 3 mg/kg, n=19; garetosmab 10 mg/kg, n=23). The mean age was 26·6 years (SD 6·8); 38 (60%) participants were female and 25 (40%) male. 62 participants completed 56 weeks of treatment; one participant in the placebo group discontinued at 53 weeks. The total number of new heterotopic bone lesions was significantly lower with garetosmab: there were 19 lesions with placebo versus one lesion with garetosmab 3 mg/kg (rate ratio vs placebo: 0·06 [95% CI 0·00-0·73]; p=0·027) and two lesions with garetosmab 10 mg/kg (rate ratio vs placebo: 0·10 [0·01-0·76]; p=0·026). Treatment-emergent AESIs occurred in one (5%) of 21 participants receiving placebo, zero of 19 receiving garetosmab 3 mg/kg, and four (17%) of 23 receiving garetosmab 10 mg/kg; all were considered treatment-related. No deaths occurred.
sections.conclusion: Garetosmab substantially reduced the number of new heterotopic bone lesions, providing robust evidence of its potential to be an efficacious and generally well tolerated disease-modifying therapy for FOP.

items.title: Immunogenicity of fractional one-fifth and one-half doses of 17DD yellow fever vaccine compared with full dose in children aged 9-23 months in Uganda: a phase 4, single-blind, randomised clinical trial.

sections.objective: Fractional doses of yellow fever vaccines have been shown to be safe and immunogenic in randomised controlled trials in adults and children. However, little evidence still remains in children younger than 2 years. We assessed immunogenicity of one-fifth (0·1 mL) and one-half (0·25 mL) fractional doses compared with full doses of 17DD yellow fever vaccine in children aged 9-23 months in Kampala, Uganda.
sections.methods: This phase 4, single-blind, randomised clinical trial evaluating fractional dose 17DD yellow fever vaccine among children was conducted at three public-sector health facilities in Uganda. Eligible participants were aged 9-23 months at enrolment, had no history of yellow fever disease or vaccination, and did not meet the exclusion criteria. Children were enrolled in three age strata: 9-12 months, 13-18 months, and 19-23 months, and were randomly assigned (1:1:1) using block randomisation (block sizes of three and six) to one-fifth (0·1 mL), one-half (0·25 mL), or full (0·5 mL) doses of the 17DD yellow fever vaccine. Participants were followed up at 4 weeks (visit 1 [V1]), 1 year (visit 2 [V2]), and 13-48 months (visit 3 [V3]) after vaccination. The primary analysis included per-protocol participants who attended within the prespecified visit window; an intention-to-treat analysis was also conducted including all randomly assigned participants with available outcome data. Participants with missing serological data were excluded from the analysis at the corresponding visit. The primary outcome was non-inferiority in seroconversion (5 percentage-point margin) at V1 measured by 50% plaque reduction neutralisation test. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03725618, and is complete.
sections.results: Between March 26, 2019, and May 11, 2021, 1784 participants were randomly assigned to either one-fifth dose (n=600), one-half dose (n=594), or full dose (n=590). The median (IQR) age at enrolment was 13 (11-18) months. Both fractional doses met the non-inferiority criterion compared with the full dose with no difference in seroconversion between one-fifth and full doses and -0·17 (95% CI -0·52 to 0·17) difference between one-half and full doses in the per-protocol population at V1. There was no difference between the one-fifth and full doses.
sections.conclusion: Both fractional doses of 17DD yellow fever vaccine were non-inferior to full doses in inducing initial seroconversion. The results support the use of fractional dose yellow fever vaccines among young children for outbreak response during supply shortages.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of litifilimab in cutaneous lupus erythematosus: 24-week results of the randomized phase 2 study, AMETHYST.

sections.objective: Cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE) is a serious autoimmune disease with no approved targeted treatments. Evaluate the efficacy and safety of litifilimab in AMETHYST Part A (Phase 2).
sections.methods: AMETHYST is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase 2/3 study that investigates litifilimab in participants with CLE. Participants were randomized to receive litifilimab 225 mg or placebo every 4 weeks during Weeks 0-24. The primary endpoint was the Cutaneous Lupus Activity Investigator's Global Assessment-Revised (CLA-IGA-R) erythema score of 0-1 at Week 16, with several Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus Disease Area and Severity Index (CLASI)-based endpoints at Week 24 as secondary endpoints. Safety was also assessed.
sections.results: Significantly more participants treated with litifilimab achieved clear/almost clear skin (CLA-IGA-R erythema 0-1) than those treated with placebo at Week 16 (14.7% vs 2.9%, P= .0263). Additionally, more participants treated with litifilimab achieved CLASI-70 response vs placebo at Week 24 (21.7% vs 5.8%, P = .0195). Litifilimab was generally well tolerated; safety data were consistent with prior studies.
sections.conclusion: Litifilimab treatment led to greater improvements in skin disease activity vs placebo and was well tolerated in participants with CLE through Week 24.
sections.other: Study was not powered to detect statistically significant differences in secondary endpoints.

items.title: Effect of clarithromycin on the circulating inflammatory proteome in community-acquired pneumonia: a secondary analysis of the ACCESS trial.

sections.objective: The ACCESS randomized double-blind controlled trial in hospitalized adults with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) showed that adding clarithromycin to standard-of-care therapy accelerated clinical recovery within the first 72 hours after the commencement of treatment and reduced progression to organ dysfunction.
sections.methods: Serum samples obtained from ACCESS trial patients at baseline and 72 hours were profiled using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel. Patients were grouped by treatment arm and by achievement of the trial's composite primary endpoint. After quality control, 70 proteins from 394 paired samples across 197 patients were analyzed to assess differential expression within and between groups over time, evaluate associations with clinical outcomes, and identify immune endotypes using unsupervised clustering.
sections.results: IL6 was selectively downregulated on day 4 in the clarithromycin arm, whereas IFN-γ, CXCL9, CXCL10, and SCF decreased over time across both treatment arms, consistent with resolution of inflammation. Among patients achieving the primary endpoint, IL6, CXCL9, CXCL10, and IFN-γ were suppressed only in clarithromycin-treated individuals. Clustering consistently identified two inflammatory endotypes with comparable SOFA, but distinct RSS scores. The endotype with lower RSS demonstrated higher IFN-γ and globally elevated inflammatory protein expression; in that endotype 90-day mortality was decreased with clarithromycin treatment.
sections.conclusion: Clarithromycin exerts measurable immunomodulatory effects in CAP, characterized by attenuation of pro-inflammatory cytokines, particularly IL6. The identification of distinct inflammatory endotypes suggests biological heterogeneity in CAP and supports future investigation of endotype-guided approaches to identify patients most likely to benefit from immunomodulatory therapies.
sections.other: Does clarithromycin treatment modulate the circulating inflammatory protein profile in CAP, and can inflammatory endotypes identify patient subgroups with distinct clinical responses?

items.title: Retrieval of Thrombosed Inferior Vena Cava Filter and Mechanical Thrombectomy of Associated Caval Thrombosis Using FlowTriever and ClotTriever Systems With the ClotTriever as Embolic Protection.
items.abstract: A 55-year-old Chinese male with anti-phospholipid syndrome presented with left lower limb deep venous thrombosis (DVT) on warfarin and had an inferior vena cava filter (IVCF) implanted before a radical resection of a perineal sarcoma. The inferior vena cava (IVC) filter removal was attempted 2 weeks after the surgery, but thrombus was found at the filter. It was decided to leave the filter and to continue with anticoagulation. He presented with progressive right lower limb swelling, erythema and pain, with a CT venogram showing caval thrombosis extending from the IVC filter to the right below-knee veins. In view of worsening symptoms, endovenous mechanical thrombectomy of the IVC and iliofemoral veins, as well as caval filter removal, was performed using the ClotTriever and FlowTriever devices (Inari Medical, US). The ClotTriever itself was then placed alongside a 16Fr internal jugular vein (IJV) sheath to remove the thrombosed filter. The FlowTriever disc was next deployed from jugular access as proximal embolic protection during the thrombectomy procedure. The procedure was successful with no symptoms of pulmonary embolism (PE). This report illustrates the alternative use of the ClotTriever BOLD as an intra-operative proximal embolic protection in the absence of alternative devices like a ProTrieve sheath, during caval thrombectomy and removal for caval thrombosis secondary to an IVC filter.Clinical ImpactThe ClotTriever BOLD catheter, deployed alongside a large retrograde sheath may be considered as an proximal embolic protection for removing thrombosed IVCFs, where there is patient with a suitably sized IVC and when alternative and appropriate devices are unavailable.

items.title: Comparison of mid-term outcomes of different patch types for endarterectomy of the common femoral artery. Secondary analysis from the ARISTON multicentre registry.

sections.objective: We sought to analyze patients who underwent femoral endarterectomy (FEA) for common femoral artery disease (CFAD) within the multicentre ARISTON registry aiming to compare the short-term and mid-term outcomes based on the use of different patch materials.
sections.methods: The study is a secondary analysis of patients from a retrospective multicentre observational registry of FEA with patch angioplasty, extracted the ARISTON collaborative. The primary endpoint of the study was clinically-driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR).
sections.results: A total of 547 patients undergoing FEA with patch angioplasty were included in the analysis and stratified according to the patch material into three groups: (i) prosthetic patch or PP (group A, n=249), (ii) bovine pericardium patch or BPP (group B, n=262), and (iii) great saphenous vein patch or GSVP (group C, n=36). Baseline characteristics differed significantly among groups. Technical success of the FEA procedure was achieved in all cases. Perioperative mortality was low and not significantly different between groups. Kaplan-Meier estimates of freedom from CD-TLR at two years were 86.2% (95% CI, 80.8-90.2%) in the PP group, 88.9% (95% CI, 83.1-92.8%) in the BPP group, and 69.8% (95% CI, 49.3-83.3%) in the GSVP group, with no statistically significant difference between groups (log-rank p=0.067). In multivariable analysis for freedom from CD-TLR, neither BPP (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.47-1.29; P=0.330) nor GSVP (HR 1.99, 95% CI 0.95-4.17; P=0.069) was significantly associated with the outcome.
sections.conclusion: In this contemporary multicentre real-world experience, PP and BPP were the most used materials for patch reconstruction after FEA in patients with primary CFAD. Although the distribution of baseline risk factors was different between groups, mid-term freedom from CD-TLR was not significantly different between-groups. The findings describe contemporary surgeon-selected practice but do not determine the optimal allocation strategy, thereby reinforcing a clinically relevant message for contemporary vascular surgery: appropriate patient selection, meticulous technical execution, and comprehensive revascularization strategy are the key drivers of clinical outcomes, whereas patch material should likely be regarded as a complementary component within an individualized reconstructive framework.

items.title: Asymptomatic vs. Symptomatic Carotid Revascularization: A Single Institution Retrospective Review.

sections.objective: While carotid revascularization reduces stroke risk in both asymptomatic (AD) and symptomatic (SD) carotid disease, its role continues to evolve with advances in medical therapy, surgical techniques, and cost considerations.
sections.methods: This retrospective study reviews outcomes of patients undergoing revascularization at a level one stroke center between 2019 and 2024. Primary endpoints were ipsilateral stroke, myocardial infarction, and death at 30-day, 90-day, and 1-year. Secondary endpoints include restenosis rates.
sections.results: 113 patients underwent 127 carotid endarterectomies. Sixty-four percent presented with SD, with a median time to intervention of 9 days (IQR 6-11). SD patients had a longer median length of stay (2 vs 1 day, p = 0.076. Follow-up rates were higher in AD at 1 year (65% vs 36%, p = 0.003). MI rates were 0% at 30- and 90-day and 0.9% at 1-year. Stroke rates were 0.9%, 0.9%, and 1.8% at 30-day, 90-day, and one year, with no difference between AD vs SD. 1-year mortality rates were 0.9% and 5.3% at 90-day and one year, without a difference by AD vs SD. Restenosis occurred in 4% of patients, with no difference between groups.
sections.conclusion: Carotid endarterectomy was associated with low perioperative rates of ipsilateral stroke, MI, and death. Despite a longer LOS, SD patients did not have significantly different outcomes or restenosis rates. While males had improved follow-up rates, there was no significant difference in outcomes by gender or race. These findings support favorable outcomes following CEA in both AD and SD.

items.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) and the choroidal challenge: A comprehensive review of AI applications in choroidal imaging.
items.abstract: The choroid is a densely vascular layer that sustains the outer retina and may reflect systemic microvascular health. With the advent of new imaging techniques, choroidal imaging has become increasingly detailed, generating vast data volumes. Conventional analytic tools often fall short in managing these high-dimensional datasets. Artificial intelligence (AI) automatically enhances, segments, and analyzes choroidal images, facilitating the discovery of choroidal biomarkers relevant to ocular and systemic disease. Yet, anatomical complexity, heterogeneous protocols, and a lack of large, annotated datasets hinder AI adoption. Overcoming these barriers is essential to assess AI-derived choroidal biomarkers as reliable diagnostic and prognostic tools.

items.title: Midterm Outcomes of the Minos Ultralow Profile Endograft: Results from the Multicentre MINER Registry.

sections.objective: The aim of this study was to assess midterm outcomes of the ultralow profile Minos endograft in a physician initiated registry.
sections.methods: A non-sponsored registry collected consecutive patients treated with the Minos device in 20 Italian centres (2021 - 2025). Elective patients (the primary analysis population) were stratified by access quality (hostile vs. standard access); hostile iliac-femoral access was defined by a narrowest iliac diameter 1.6, aortic bifurcation diameter < 16 mm, or severe circumferential calcification. Proximal neck features were covariates only; urgent and emergent procedures were analysed separately. Outcomes were thirty day technical success, mortality, and major adverse events (MAEs), and midterm freedom from rupture, limb occlusion, type I or III endoleak, and re-intervention.
sections.results: Of 310 patients (mean aneurysm diameter 54.8 ± 10.0 mm), 288 (92.9%) were elective. Among these, 154 (53.5%) had a standard access and 134 (46.5%) a hostile access. The latter were more frequently women (16.4% vs. 6.0%; p = .009) and more frequently had peripheral arterial disease (31.6% vs. 16.8%; p = .006). Elective technical success was 100%, with no thirty day deaths. The thirty day MAE rate was higher with hostile access (8.2% vs. 1.3%; p = .032), mainly from access related events and blood loss > 1 000 mL (3.7% vs. 0.0%; p = .021), as was early re-intervention (3.7% vs. 0.0%; p = .021). At 3 years there were no aneurysm related deaths; freedom from limb occlusion was 97% vs. 100% (p = .025) and from type I OR III endoleak was 98% vs. 100% (p = .18) in the standard and hostile access groups, respectively.
sections.conclusion: The Minos ultralow profile endograft was safe and effective for the treatment of elective abdominal aortic aneurysms. Peri-operative morbidity was higher when the iliac-femoral access was hostile, and limb occlusion, type I - III endoleak, and re-intervention were more evident compared with standard access anatomy. An ultralow profile platform can extend endovascular repair to unfavourable access vessels without affecting midterm device performance.

items.title: Cilostazol and Risk of Major Adverse Limb and Cardiovascular Events after Revascularisation for Peripheral Artery Disease.

sections.objective: Patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) remain at high risk of major adverse limb events (MALE) and cardiovascular events (MACE) after revascularisation. Cilostazol, a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor with antiplatelet and antiproliferative effects, reduces re-stenosis but its real world impact on clinical outcomes is uncertain. This retrospective, nationwide, propensity score matched cohort study evaluated the effectiveness and safety of cilostazol on MALE, MACE, and all cause mortality after lower limb revascularisation for PAD.
sections.methods: Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database, patients who underwent lower limb revascularisation for PAD from 2010 - 2023, with follow up through 2024 were identified. Patients with prior cilostazol use were excluded. 1:1 propensity score matching (n = 5 464 per group) adjusted for baseline differences. Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing risk models were used to evaluate outcomes. The comparison reflects cilostazol used with or without background antithrombotic therapy.
sections.results: Cilostazol use was associated with significantly lower risks of MALE (78.7 vs. 154.0 events/1 000 person-years; subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 0.50; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.46 - 0.53) and MACE (97.9 vs. 117.1 events/1 000 person-years; hazard ratio [HR] 0.84; 95% CI 0.79 - 0.89). All cause mortality was also reduced (116.0 vs. 127.6 events/1 000 person-years; HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.86 - 0.96). Major bleeding did not differ significantly between groups (SHR 0.90; 95% CI 0.81 - 1.00), although the absolute rate was high in both groups (12.1% vs. 13.1%). Subgroup analysis showed greater limb benefit in patients not on other antiplatelet agents.
sections.conclusion: Cilostazol after PAD revascularisation was associated with lower risks of limb and cardiovascular events and mortality. These effects were observed without any increase in the rate of major bleeding, although this rate was high in both groups. Randomised trials focused on cardiovascular events are needed.

items.title: Differences in Clinical Presentation of Chronic Pelvic Pain Caused by Iliac Vein Obstruction Impacts Referral Pathway, Time to Diagnosis, and Post-stenting Pain Resolution.

sections.objective: Iliac venous stenting improves chronic pelvic pain (CPP) caused by iliac vein obstruction (IVO). Signs and symptoms vary, but this pain is reproducible and easily identifiable. However, patients can experience significant delays in diagnosis and treatment. This study aimed to determine associations between the referral history, clinical presentation, pain characteristics, and stenting outcomes among women with CPP due to IVO.
sections.methods: This was a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data of women who were referred to a vascular surgeon with signs and symptoms of IVO, including CPP, and who underwent iliac venous stenting. Associations between clinical presentation (signs, symptoms, pain severity), medical and referral history, and stenting outcomes were compared between three patient groups based on number of other specialist consultations prior to stenting (none, one, or at least two).
sections.results: Data were for 113 women (46.5 ± 15.7 years) who had CPP for 6.3 ± 6.6 years with initial severity of 6.7 ± 2.3 (out of 10). CPP was reproducible for all women, with exercise, standing, and intercourse being the most common triggers. More than two thirds had lower limb pain, oedema, and varicose veins. At a median of 7 years post-stenting, the latest pain score was 0.8 ± 1.6, and approximately 80% had full pain resolution. Women who had seen at least two other specialists had the worst initial pelvic pain, the most prescription pain medication, back pain, other abdominopelvic signs and symptoms, and previous interventions, and the fewest varicose veins. These women had 8.5 ± 7.9 years to diagnosis, but 99% still had significant improvement in, and 66% had full resolution of, their pelvic pain.
sections.conclusion: All patients had a reproducible pattern of venous origin pelvic pain, but those with worse CPP, more abdominopelvic symptoms, and less varicose veins had a more complex and delayed referral pathway and the lowest pain resolution.

items.title: Long Term Results of Surgical Treatment of Chronic Venous Thoracic Outlet Syndrome: A Single Centre Experience.

sections.objective: This retrospective cohort study with cross-sectional analysis aimed to evaluate the surgical and long term functional outcomes of a structured treatment algorithm for patients with chronic venous thoracic outlet syndrome (cVTOS).
sections.methods: Patients with cVTOS and treated at this tertiary centre between 2016 and 2024 were included. Treatment consisted of transaxillary thoracic outlet decompression (TOD), venolysis, and subclavian vein (SCV) recanalisation. In case of persistent venous obstruction during the primary procedure, anticipated repeat percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) was planned. Anticoagulation (rivaroxaban) was prescribed until 48 hours before surgery, resumed the day after surgery for six weeks, or until 48 hours before re-PTA. The primary endpoint included SCV patency and secondary outcomes included functional outcomes (DASH and Derkash scores).
sections.results: Seventy patients were included (mean age 35 years; 56% women). Median time to presentation was 40 (20.0 - 104.0) months after initial upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (UEDVT). Eleven patients (16%) had an operative complication (haematoma n = 6, pneumothorax n = 1, UEDVT n = 1, transient Horner syndrome n = 1, phrenic nerve injury n = 1, and SCV rupture n = 1). Median length of hospital stay was 1.0 day. Venography post-TOD/PTA showed persistent venous obstruction in 15 patients (21%) for which re-PTA was planned. Over time, 20 patients (29%) developed re-stenosis. A total of 35 (50%) re-PTAs were performed. Primary patency was 56%, primary assisted patency was 86%, and secondary patency was 93% at last follow up (12 months). Median post-operative DASH score decreased significantly (pre-op: 32.9 (15.8 - 48.3) vs. post-op 8.0 (2.3 - 27.8); p < .001) with a mean follow up of 45.7 ± 27.5 months. Zero patients reported a poor Derkash score.
sections.conclusion: Chronic VTOS can be effectively treated with good long term functional outcomes. Re-PTAs were necessary in half of the cases (anticipated). This treatment algorithm diminished the need of secondary interventions in 50% of the cases, as well as the need for long term anticoagulation usage.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of camrelizumab plus docetaxel and carboplatin as neoadjuvant therapy for stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer: the HELEN-Trio 011 randomized clinical trial.

sections.objective: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy has become the standard-of-care for stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC); however, anthracycline-containing regimens are associated with considerable toxicity. We evaluated camrelizumab combined with an anthracycline-free docetaxel-carboplatin regimen in this setting.
sections.methods: We performed a multicenter, randomized, open-label, phase 3 trial at 14 hospitals in China between December 2022 and June 2025. Eligible patients were women aged 18-70 years with previously untreated, stage II-III TNBC. Patients were randomized 2:1 to receive 6 cycles of neoadjuvant docetaxel (75 mg/m2) plus carboplatin (area under the curve [AUC]=6) on day 1, with or without camrelizumab (200 mg intravenously on day 3). The primary endpoint was pathological complete response (pCR), defined as ypT0/Tis ypN0, evaluated in the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population (all patients who received at least one dose of study treatment).
sections.results: A total of 369 patients were enrolled, and 352 comprised the mITT population for efficacy analysis. The pCR rate was 57.5% (134/233) in the camrelizumab-chemotherapy group and 45.4% (54/119) in the chemotherapy-alone group, corresponding to an absolute difference of 12.2% (95% CI, 1.4 to 22.9; one-sided P=0.014). Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 24.9% (58/233) in the camrelizumab-chemotherapy group and 21.8% (26/119) in the chemotherapy-alone group. No treatment-related deaths were reported.
sections.conclusion: The addition of camrelizumab to neoadjuvant docetaxel plus carboplatin significantly increased the pCR rate in patients with stage II-III TNBC, with a manageable safety profile. This regimen represents a promising anthracycline-free strategy that warrants comparison with current standard chemoimmunotherapy .

items.title: EARLY STROKE AFTER AORTIC ARCH REPAIR: COMPARATIVE AND PROPORTIONAL META-ANALYSES OF OPEN, HYBRID, AND TOTAL ENDOVASCULAR STRATEGIES.

sections.objective: Early stroke remains one of the most devastating complications after aortic arch repair. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated early stroke after open, hybrid, and total endovascular aortic arch repair using separate comparative and proportional frameworks.
sections.methods: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through July 27, 2026. Observational studies reporting neurological outcomes after adult open, hybrid, or total endovascular aortic arch repair were included. The primary comparative meta-analysis pooled propensity score-matched or weighted studies comparing hybrid with open repair using random-effects restricted maximum likelihood models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Separate proportional random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled stroke incidences for each strategy. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and the Joanna. Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261461659).
sections.results: Thirty-four studies were included. Seven propensity score-matched or weighted cohorts comprising 948 patients (474 open and 474 hybrid repairs) contributed to the primary comparative meta-analysis. No significant difference in early stroke was identified between hybrid and open repair (OR 1.99, 95% CI 0.46-8.58; P=.292; I2=52.9%). Post hoc comparative analyses restricted to dissection cohorts (3 cohorts; 572 patients) and Zone 0 hybrid repair (3 cohorts; 448 patients) were also inconclusive and highly imprecise. In descriptive proportional analyses, pooled early-stroke incidences were 5.3% after open, 7.5% after hybrid, and 6.4% after total endovascular repair. Technique-stratified incidences were 6.1% for conventional open repair, 4.4% for open repair with frozen elephant trunk, and 5.3% for branched total endovascular repair.
sections.conclusion: Adjusted comparative evidence showed no significant difference in early stroke between hybrid and open aortic arch repair. Evidence for total endovascular repair remains predominantly non-comparative. Treatment should be individualised according to aortic pathology, urgency, anatomy, operative risk, and institutional expertise.

items.title: ArtAssist Sequential Compression Biomechanical Device as a Cost-Dominant Limb-Salvage Strategy for No-Option Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia: A Decade and Half, Single-Centre Cohort Study with Health Economic and Q-TWiST Analysis.

sections.objective: Major lower limb amputation for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) costs the Irish Health Service Executive (HSE) a median €88,820 per patient; long-term health economic and quality-adjusted survival evidence for ArtAssist SCBD is lacking.
sections.methods: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with non-reconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary centre (January 2008-June 2025). Primary endpoints were limb salvage, cost-effectiveness versus primary amputation, and Q-TWiST. Kaplan-Meier analysis of limb salvage, multivariable Cox regression for major amputation, competing-risks analysis, and health economic modelling using contemporaneous cost data were performed.
sections.results: Overall crude limb salvage, defined as freedom from major amputation, was achieved in 85% (294/347 patients). At last follow-up, 48% of patients were alive without major amputation. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year limb salvage at 95%. The cumulative incidence of major amputation at 5 years was 8% when accounting for death as a competing event, confirming durable limb preservation despite substantial long-term mortality in this elderly, comorbid population. Male sex, hypertension, and ischaemic heart disease independently predicted major amputation or limb-salvage failure (HRs 1·70, 1·80, 1·71; all P ≤ ·012). Comorbidity burden showed a dose-response relationship (P = ·008). 90-day rental (€1,373/patient) reduced total expenditure six-fold versus primary amputation (€5·3M vs €30·8M), saving €76,500/patient. Q-TWiST yielded a gain of 3·37 QALYs per patient; ICER €21,900/QALY confirms a dominant strategy.
sections.conclusion: ArtAssist SCBD achieves a six-fold reduction in costs versus primary amputation, +3·37 QALYs/patient, and an ICER of €21,900/QALY a dominant strategy supported by durable limb preservation, with 85% overall crude limb salvage and an estimated 5-year limb salvage of approximately 95% in the largest single-centre cohort reported. These findings support universal commissioning of ArtAssist SCBD for non-reconstructible CLTI.

items.title: Implementation of the Universal Femoral Access Protocol Decreases Complications of Peripheral Vascular Interventions.

sections.objective: Common femoral artery (CFA) is the most common access site for peripheral vascular interventions (PVI). Ultrasound (US) use has been shown to decrease access-related complications. However, the recommended site for femoral artery puncture has not been well defined, and the access technique varies significantly based on the operator specialty and training.
